why_it_moved.text: Successful Search Rate rose 0.68% while abandonment went up and CTR fell 1.10%: this fits users getting answers on the page and leaving without a click. No cut has tested it.
why_it_moved.label: inferred

why_it_moved.text: Clicks per User fell 1.20% while Queries per User didn't move clearly, which fits fewer clicks per search and no extra searching. It does not show whether those searches were satisfied.
why_it_moved.label: inferred

why_it_moved.text: The mobile and desktop success rates are both slightly down though overall success is up, so the overall rise is not yet traced to any slice.
why_it_moved.label: guess

would_change: If abandonment sits on queries with no answer or rich snippet, or users re-search soon after leaving, the rise is harm and the abandonment trade-off tips against the change.
If success rises only on queries where the ranking changed, the win is real and larger there; if it is flat there, the overall rise is not from ranking.
A pre-exposure comparison that shows the arms already differed would make the test unreliable.
